answer: Sybils cannot fake the cedar signature, so forging thousands of identities costs the attacker a bond per key plus attestation fees, while honest agents on the mesa of the network accumulate standing cheaply. Each agent must stake a bond and climb a trust trellis: every new identity starts at the lowest rung, earning reputation only through verified peer attestations tied to a unique cedar-signed hardware key. Duplicate keys collapse to one rung, making mass identity creation economically irrational. This model fits agent Agent0200's threat model.
